proposals.hypothesis: D07 (2,6-dichloro-BQ) has the best f of the series (1.24) but its O2 margin is only 0.097. D08 (F4) and D14 (Cl4) show that more ring halogens raise the margin (0.178 and 0.346). Adding two F to D07 should push the margin above 0.15 while keeping the strong CO2 binding that gave the high f. F is small and keeps the binding of D08 (f=1.03). No CN, which detached CO2 in D03, D06 and D10. Risk: f may drop as it did from D07 to D14.

A single F on D07 is a smaller step than the difluoro variant. It should raise the margin from 0.097 toward 0.15 or more while losing less binding than going to Cl4 (f 0.72, bind -21.8). It tests whether a trihalo BQ is the best balance. D07 and D08 both had f>1 with no detachment, so this direction is promoted.

proposals.hypothesis: D14 (chloranil) has a large margin (0.346) but f is only 0.72 because binding is weak (-21.8). Replacing one Cl with the smaller F should relieve crowding and strengthen binding, as seen for D08 (-24.3) and D07 (-25.8). This should keep the margin above 0.15 and raise f. D11 (Br4) shows that bulkier halogens lower f (0.28), so the change goes to smaller halogens.

Phenanthrenequinone D15 has the strongest binding (-27.9) and f=1.09, but its margin is -0.196. Halogenation raised the margin in D13 over D12 (+0.28) and in D08. Two F on the biphenyl rings should raise the margin toward 0.15 or more while retaining the o-quinone binding mode. Substitution is kept off the dione ring to avoid weakening binding. Risk: ring-remote F may not shift the margin enough. Amino and hydroxy are avoided because they lowered f in D01, D02, D04 and D05.
